meta.title: Online Retail II: sales snapshot
meta.source: Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository, CC BY 4.0
meta.yearNote: Years are calendar years: 2009 covers December only and 2011 ends on 9 December.
meta.additivity: Orders and customers are distinct counts. Orders add up across months and countries (an invoice has one date and one country) but not across categories, because one invoice can contain several; the category filter is single-select. Customers never add up across months or countries.
cleaningRules: Non-product stock codes removed (postage, manual entries, discounts, samples, fees, adjustments, test lines, gift vouchers).
Lines with price <= 0 or quantity 0, and negative quantities outside cancellations, removed.
Sales of 10,000+ units cancelled at once, with their cancellations, and lines priced above 100x their code's median removed.
Cancellations ("C" invoices) kept as returns, not sales.
Lines without a Customer ID count in revenue and orders, not in customer metrics.
Revenue = Quantity x Price in GBP, no currency conversion.

rfmRules.scores: R (days since last order, fewer is better), F (orders) and M (revenue) are scored 1-5 by quintile of rank (rank-first). FM = (F + M) / 2 rounded half up.

meta.cohortRule: Cohort = month of a customer's first order; country = that order's country. Share = customers ordering N months later / cohort size.
meta.productSpanRule: For all countries and the top-5 countries, every contiguous span of calendar years has its product count, an exact top 200 and a Pareto curve: curve[i] is the share of revenue from the top (i + 1)% of products by revenue. Other countries have per-year top 200s only.
meta.basketRule: Top 10 products by revenue per scope. share = orders containing both / all orders in the scope.
